# Kuṇḍakakucchisindhavajātaka (Ja 254)

**ID:** Ja 254
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Kuṇḍakakucchisindhavajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kuṇḍakakucchisindhavajātaka* is the 254th story in the canonical Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1879]. According to the commentary, the Buddha related this story while residing at the Jetavana monastery in Sāvatthī in connection with the Elder Sāriputta, opening with the verse line *Bhutvā tiṇaparighāsaṁ* ("Grass and the scum of gruel") [Fausböll 1879]. In modern ethical and socio-religious discussions of the Pali canon, the story is highlighted as an illustration of the immediate temporal and material rewards of giving (*dāna*): an impoverished elderly woman who gives what modest food she has to Sāriputta receives sudden, immense financial rewards and wealth amounting to a hundred thousand coins from donors including Anāthapiṇḍika, Visākhā, and the king, before being established in the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpatti*) [Fenn 1994; Fausböll 1879]. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta appears as a noble thoroughbred colt reared on rice-powder by the old woman [Rotman 2017; Fausböll 1879].

Andy Rotman notes that an episode in the Sanskrit *Divyāvadāna* regarding the reception of monks' bowls bears narrative similarity to the *Kuṇḍakakucchisindhavajātaka* [Rotman 2017]. Within Pali literature, the story is closely linked with the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, where DharmaNexus detects substantial textual reuse (sharing passages across multiple segments), corroborated by modern index references to the Jātaka in the commentary [Burlingame 1921; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-collection parallels with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* itself as well as machine-aligned correspondences with the Tibetan *Karmaśataka* (*las brgya tham pa*) [DharmaNexus].

- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): ལས་བརྒྱ་ཐམ་པ (karmaṣataka) (D0340) [bo]
